hero.tagline: The full-stack Go framework for Gophers.
intro: Write the backend in Go and the pages in React. Tifa compiles the whole site into one executable that you copy to a small VPS and run. No Node in production, no process manager, no reverse proxy, no Redis.

It is for Go developers whose business logic and data already live in Go, who want to write pages with the React ecosystem, and who do not want to keep a Node service running in production just for server-side rendering.
hero.status: Tifa is very early. APIs will change, and many compiler optimizations are not done yet.

demo.title: What it looks like
demo.intro: One folder per page. Go loads the data, React shows it:

rows: The Go HTTP server in the binary, which gets its own Let's Encrypt certificate and speaks HTTP/2
TanStack Router, rendered by a [pure Go QuickJS](https://github.com/liustack/slowjs) inside the Go process
An in-process render memo for pages, a CDN in front if you want one, plus whatever you keep in Go memory
SQLite, with a [pure Go driver](https://github.com/liustack/sqlite) so CGO stays off

numbers.title: One small server is enough
numbers.memo: The **[render memo](/docs/reference/memo)** is on for every page, signed-in ones like a cart or a bill included. Every request fetches fresh data first and reuses the last render only when nothing changed, so a page is never stale. A render is reused only for the same data and the same session, so one person's page never reaches another. The app writes no caching code.
numbers.visits: Whole visits, played back from real browsers on the example shop: shoppers, staff and crawlers on one server at once, every server as shipped and warmed up with the same visits first (2026-11-18).
numbers.caption: Throughput at 8 concurrent sessions with no pause between pages, the median of 3 rounds:

rows.tifaNoMemo: For reference: Tifa with the render memo off
rows.tanstackGzip: For reference: TanStack Start with gzip
rows.nextNoPrefetch: For reference: Next.js with prefetch off

numbers.definition: A full load is a request the server answers with a whole page: the landing of a visit, and a search or another action that loads a page. A client navigation is one the router answers with data alone. Every server plays the same visits, so about a third of the page views of every row are full loads.
numbers.method: The first three rows are the frameworks as shipped. Each reference row changes one setting, to show what that default costs or buys. Versions: Tifa v0.1.0, slowjs v0.31.6, Next.js 16.4.6, TanStack Start 1.169.3, Node 24.13.0. Each server on one core of a Google Cloud `t2d-standard-4` VM (AMD EPYC 7B13). [Whole visits](/docs/reference/performance#whole-visits-to-the-shop-2026-11-18) has the mix, what each default costs and what the numbers mean.
cost: Tifa renders pages in slowjs, QuickJS compiled to Go assembly. It has no JIT, so one render takes longer than in Node.

Every request renders, one at a time (2026-11-18): Next.js answers 1.17 times as many page requests as Tifa and TanStack Start 1.57 times, at 7 and 6 times Tifa's peak memory. See [the study](https://github.com/liustack/tifa/blob/v0.1.13/docs/studies/nextjs-and-tanstack-start.md#conclusions).

status.title: Status
status.note: Tifa is very early. APIs will change, and many compiler optimizations are not done yet.
status.policy: Tifa does not accept pull requests. A framework like this touches the compiler, the bundler, server rendering and developer experience at once, and a change in one pulls on the others. Getting that right takes a lot of context, so every line is written and reviewed by one author. Two ways to help:
help: **[Open an issue](https://github.com/liustack/tifa/issues/new/choose).** Bugs, ideas, confusing errors, unclear docs. A clear issue with steps to reproduce helps more than a patch, and issues shape what gets built next.
**Fork it.** Under MIT your copy is yours to change and publish. [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/liustack/tifa/blob/v0.1.13/CONTRIBUTING.md) has the notes for working on a fork.

why.title: Why it exists
text: I wanted to ship a small product on TanStack Start. My other VPSes were full, Black Friday was still weeks away and I did not feel like buying another one, so I dug out an old box with 1 CPU and 1 GB of RAM. I had Codex set up the usual stack in one go: nginx, Node.js, PM2, TanStack Start, Redis, BullMQ, cron and SQLite.
It did not really run. It crawled.
So I started hacking on Tifa. Once it is done, deploying should mean copying one Go binary to the VPS, and that is it.

start.title: Start an app
start.note: You need Go 1.27, Node 20.19 or 22.12 and later, and [pnpm](https://pnpm.io). Node only builds the front end. The executable you ship never needs it.
